messages:
anika: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection rollout at 17:30 we’re seeing a 2x increase in token-level p95 for /v1/generate. I dug into the profiler and the chosen kernels look like they’re falling back to the generic matmul path for sequences >512. screenshot in thread :point_down:

matt: Can you paste the exact query from the token-latency dashboard? Is this only on dedicated or also hosted?

jules: fyi I saw a small blip in KV cache hit rate around the same time — TTL evictions spiked on pool-a. might be correlated.

anika: Dashboard panel: `token_latency_by_position{route="/v1/generate",model="rw-1.2b"}` — overlayed before/after. Blip is cross-region but concentrated on us-west-2. Hosted and some dedicated nodes on that pool affected.

matt: ok re: kernel selection, last change toggled heuristic to pick fused-gemm for seq<=512 else generic. If seq distribution shifted slightly higher we could see more fallbacks. can we dump kernel-choice histogram from runtime?

anika: I already pulled a sampling dump: `kernel_choice_counts{kernel="fused_gemm",range="0-512"}` and `kernel_choice_counts{kernel="generic",range=">512"}` — attached small CSV. samples show 38% more generic picks post-rollout.

leo: suggestion: add a temporary override to force fused-gemm for the top 3 models for the next hour while we test, then rollback. That will tell us if kernel selection is the root cause. :thinking:

jules: also can we check KV cache miss latency? If evictions force recompute of prefixes that could amplify token cost. `kv_cache_hit_rate{pool="pool-a"}` dropped from 98% -> 90% at the same time.

anika: created a quick A/B on one replica to force fused-gemm. early signs: token p95 improved ~30% on that replica. putting this into an experiment doc now.

matt: good. create an alert rule for aggregate burn rate so paging only happens when cost and impact warrant it. we almost paged ops for a noisy 10% dev queue before confirming root cause.

jules: proposed alert (prom-style):
```
- alert: TokenLatencyBurnRateHigh
  expr: increase(token_latency_seconds_sum[5m]) / increase(token_latency_seconds_count[5m]) > 0.5
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "Token-level burn rate high for {{ $labels.route }}"
    runbook: "https://redwood.internal/runbooks/token-burn"
```
Note: that expr is illustrative — could use burn rate math comparing to SLO baseline.

leo: for paging thresholds we should use a two-stage policy: 1) auto-warning alert at 10% burn-rate over SLO (email/cc channel), 2) page if burn-rate >30% for 15m or if error budget depletion velocity > threshold. keep noise low.

infra-bot: deploy v2026.3.7 started for runtime/kernels at 17:28 by matt — step 3/6: kernel-selection tweak applied.

anika: current plan: 1) run fuse-gemm override on a small canary (done), 2) add kernel-choice histogram + kv-cache-hit metric panels to per-route dashboard, 3) add the two-stage alerts (warning + page), 4) bake results 60m then decide rollback/adjust heuristics.

matt: +1. can someone open a small ticket in eng-runtime with the experiment artifacts and link the dashboard panels? Jules?

jules: done — https://redwood.kanban/ISSUE-4827 added with profiler CSV, sample traces, and dashboard links.

anika: quick ops note for runbook: include snippet to temporarily override kernel selection:```sh
# on runtime control plane
redwoodctl runtime set-kernel-override --model rw-1.2b --kernel fused_gemm --duration 1h --reason "investigate post-rollout p95"
```

ops-pager: paging policy acknowledged. if the page goes out I’ll want: affected route, p95 delta, kv cache hit rate, and a recent profiler snapshot.

matt: ok will wait for 45m of data after canary. if fused override fixes it we’ll schedule a patch to the heuristic and add regression tests for seq distribution.

anika: leaving the canary running — will post follow-up with consolidated numbers and panel links in ~30–45m. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
